the development and evaluation of novel signal processing techniques for the analysis of EEG signals.
the identification of cognitively relevant EEG features and their sonification for the purpose of visualizing and analyzing the EEG.
the identification and analysis of discriminative features for the EEG signal which is a crucial step for the correlation with cognitive processes.

our new methods are well-suited for the analysis of EEG signals from psycholinguistic studies.

the ICA features are well suited for the analysis of the speech perception and the speech perception of the EEG signals.

the proposed methods are able to extract features which can be used to distinguish between different cognitive processes.

we are able to extract features that are highly correlated with the cognitive processes that are being investigated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ICA can be a powerful tool for feature extraction and feature selection for the analysis of EEG data.
the combination of ICA with nonparametric source modelling provides a powerful framework for the analysis of EEG signals in psycholinguistic studies.
the combination of ICA and sonification provides an interesting and powerful tool for the analysis and visualization of EEG signals in psycholinguistic research and beyond.
